findings.reasoning: C-45 (AISI 1045) is a medium-carbon steel with ~0.45% carbon. 'Toughening' (quench and temper) to only 24–32 HRC requires a very high tempering temperature that essentially over-tempers this grade, making it difficult to achieve consistently; such low hardness from quench-and-temper is normally specified for low-carbon or alloy steels. The designer should verify whether normalizing or a different target hardness range was intended.
findings.correction: Review the required hardness against C-45 hardenability data. Either change the material to a low-carbon/alloy steel suited to 24–32 HRC toughening, or adjust the hardness specification to a range appropriate for quenched-and-tempered C-45 (typically ≥40 HRC before high temper, or specify normalizing if ~200 HB / ~20 HRC is acceptable).

findings.rule: Tolerance tighter than standard machining process capability
findings.reasoning: D21 specifies 20±0.02 mm (total tolerance band 0.04 mm). The drawing's own general machining tolerance table lists ±0.1 mm for the 6-to-30 mm range, meaning this explicit tolerance is five times tighter than what the shop considers standard. Holding ±0.02 mm on a linear dimension requires precision grinding or fine boring, adding significant cost.
findings.correction: Confirm whether ±0.02 mm is functionally required (e.g., a bearing seat or press-fit length). If not, relax to ±0.05 mm or apply the general tolerance. If it is required, add a surface-finish or GD&T callout so the machinist knows to use a precision process.

findings.rule: Feature description does not match dimension types
findings.reasoning: Feature F10 is described as 'Two holes: 20±0.02 mm and 50±0.1 mm spacing', yet D21 and D22 are both recorded as type 'linear'. A hole diameter cannot be defined by a linear dimension without a diameter symbol or note. This ambiguity means the machinist cannot determine whether 20±0.02 is a hole size or a location distance.
findings.correction: Clarify F10: if 20±0.02 is a hole diameter, change D21 to type 'diameter' and add the ⌀ symbol; if it is a spacing, update the feature description to remove the word 'holes' and define the actual hole diameters separately.
